title: The Embrace in the Dark Medieval
summary: In the nights of 1242, becoming Cainite begins with being murdered by a vampire.

claims.text: A childe is told plainly that a vampire murdered the childe's mortal self.
The new Cainite keeps a human mind, memories and attachments, and still feels guilt over the first kill.

title: The War of Princes
summary: The age of the Dark Medieval in which Cainite lords war over cities while faith rules the mortal world.

claims.text: The present nights are named the War of Princes.

title: Fledglings to Methuselahs
summary: The ranks of age among Cainites in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: Methuselahs are of the Fifth and Sixth Generations, the oldest active vampires.
Methuselahs are a thousand years old or more and barely human in their thinking.
An ancilla is usually of the Tenth or Eleventh Generation, between 100 and 200 years old and hungry for power.
A neonate is a vampire under a hundred years old.

title: High and Low Clans
summary: How Cainites rank the clans in 1242: some rule, some beg, depending on city and history.

claims.text: Clans are counted High or Low depending on who rules the city, the clan's history and its deeds.
A Cainite dies into a clan and takes on its centuries of weight and sin.

title: The Clans of Caine in 1242
summary: The clans as they stand in the Dark Medieval, where what makes a clan is no longer clear.

claims.text: The Salubri trace their line to the Antediluvian Saulot, yet most no longer count them a clan.
In 1133 Tremere sorcerers raided Saulot's tomb and committed Amaranth, and their eldest became Third Generation.
Most Cainites now accept the Tremere as a clan despite how they rose.

title: The Traditions in the Dark Medieval
summary: Caine's six commandments as Cainites of 1242 know them, each with its own wording.

claims.text: The six are the Covenant, the Domain, the Progeny, the Accounting, Destruction and the Silence of the Blood.
The First Tradition, the Covenant, binds all Cainites as Caine's brood under the Traditions.
By the Second Tradition a domain is its master's concern, visitors must present themselves, and the master may hunt within it.
The Fifth Tradition forbids spilling the blood of an elder of one's kind; that right belongs to those closest to Caine.
The Sixth Tradition, the Silence of the Blood, forbids revealing one's nature to those not of the blood.

title: Prince, Sheriff and Court
summary: The offices of a Dark Medieval city's Cainite court.

claims.text: A Prince is a traditional city ruler who claims authority over the Traditions.
A Prince's Sheriff in a city like London needs a full grasp of the domain's laws.
Hunters of the Church are nearly everywhere, whatever Traditions a city keeps.

title: Generations in the Dark Medieval
summary: Distance from Caine, and what the thin-blooded of the age can do.

claims.text: The youngest vampires can rarely Embrace: without the strength the victim simply dies, and without political standing an elder may kill both.

title: The Amaranth
summary: Drinking another Cainite's heart's blood or soul for a sudden rise in power.

claims.text: The Amaranth is drinking the heart's blood or soul of another Cainite, an ethically doubtful but very effective way to gain power.

title: Ghouls and Revenants
summary: Mortals fed vitae, and the families bred from them.

claims.text: Vitae binds a servant more surely than money or fear, and most ghouls are tied by blood oath to their master.
A regnant is a vampire who keeps a ghoul; a revenant is born of a ghoul family.

title: Hunters of the Dark Medieval
summary: Mortals who hunt the Damned, made bolder in this age by the Church's wars.

claims.text: Cainites blame the Cathars for how dangerous these violent nights have become.
Hunters of the Church are almost everywhere.

title: Lupines
summary: Wild shapeshifters of the woods, feared by Cainites of every clan.

claims.text: Lupines are described as packs of wild men who turn into wolves and can tear a vampire to ashes.
Cainites are advised not to enter the woods unprepared.

title: Witches and Warlocks
summary: Humans with magical power, once revered, now feared like the Damned.

claims.text: Mortals with magic were once worshipped as servants of gods, and are now feared.

title: The Shining Ones
summary: The fae of the Dark Medieval, wild beings whose name is best not spoken.

claims.text: The Others, called the Shining Ones, live both in and outside this world, and their name should not be spoken aloud.

title: Ghosts
summary: Souls of the dead who linger instead of crossing to judgment.

claims.text: Some souls of those a vampire kills linger, to torment the killer, finish their work or guard loved ones.

title: True Faith
summary: The rare holy power of mortals whose belief goes far beyond lip service.

claims.text: Most people give faith only lip service, but a rare few believe far more deeply.

title: The Roads
summary: The moral codes of the Dark Medieval Cainites, each with its own ethics and paths.

claims.text: Most Damned spiral down, but the Roads offer a way to hold on without going mad.
Changing Road is risky, pushing the Cainite close to the Beast, and needs a mentor on the new Road.
The major Roads are Beast, Heaven, Humanity, Kings, Lilith, Metamorphosis and Sin; Bones and Yasa are minor Roads.

title: The Road of the Beast
summary: Via Bestiae: the Road that sees human society as the judge of who lives and dies, and rejects it.

claims.text: Followers see society as the force that decides who lives, starves or is called a murderer.

title: The Road of Heaven
summary: Via Caeli: the Road of those who believe divine purpose guides even the Damned.

claims.text: Followers believe divine purpose guides fate, so that even great evil may serve a greater end.

title: The Road of Humanity
summary: Via Humanitas: holding on to the person one was before death.

claims.text: Followers hold that a Cainite should remain who the Cainite was before dying, and that reinvention is a lie or a folly.

title: The Road of Kings
summary: Via Regalis: the Road of rulers, who trace their right to rule back to Caine.

claims.text: Followers trace the Road to Caine's oath that ruling in darkness beats false humility in the light; some think God mandates their rule.

title: The Road of Lilith
summary: Derech Lilit: the Road that reveres Lilith as mother, survivor and catalyst.

claims.text: By some Noddist accounts, Lilith may be older than Judaism, Christianity, Noddist scripture and even Caine.

title: The Road of Metamorphosis
summary: Via Mutationis: the Road that asks what vampires become next.

claims.text: Most who walk it are Tzimisce.

title: The Road of Sin
summary: Via Peccati: the Road of Sinners, who acknowledge no power above themselves.

claims.text: Sinners say their rebellion began with Caine's rejection of God's authority.

title: The Road of Bones
summary: Via Ossium: a minor Road concerned with remembrance and death.

claims.text: Few true records of Cainite history exist, and the eldest drift into torpor and incoherence.

title: The Road of Yasa
summary: Via Yasaq: the Anda's Road, drawn from the Mongol code of Chinghis Khan.

claims.text: The Anda's code stresses honour, respect and loyalty to family and sworn kin, and most Anda walk it.

title: Golconda
summary: A myth, a goal or a purpose: the state where a Cainite lives in balance with the Beast.

claims.text: Many Roads speak of Golconda, a state where the paragon coexists with the Beast and becomes a more perfect vampire.
To most Cainites it is a myth.

title: Assamites (Dark Ages)
summary: Judges and scholars of Alamut; traditional Assamites follow the Road of Blood.

claims.text: Assamite viziers have Auspex, Presence and Quietus (Hematus).
Each Assamite vizier is obsessed with the highest intellectual or creative Ability, which acts as a derangement.

title: Brujah (Dark Ages)
summary: Passionate idealists whose fire can turn to rage.

claims.text: Brujah have Celerity, Potence and Presence.
Rolls to resist or guide frenzy are two higher for a Brujah.

title: Cappadocians (Dark Ages)
summary: The Clan of Death: lorekeepers who study death as a mystery to be solved.

claims.text: Cappadocians have Auspex, Fortitude and Necromancy.
Cappadocians look ashen and corpselike and cannot spend vitae to seem alive.
Cappadocians are the lorekeepers and historians of the Cainites, studying death through dissection, the dead and the Underworld.

title: Gangrel (Dark Ages)
summary: Wild wanderers close to the Beast.

claims.text: Gangrel have Animalism, Fortitude and Protean.
When a Gangrel frenzies, the Beast may leave a small physical or mental animal trait.

title: Lasombra (Dark Ages)
summary: The Clan of Shadows.

claims.text: Lasombra have Dominate, Obtenebration and Potence.
Lasombra do not show in reflections and cannot abide bright light.

title: Malkavians (Dark Ages)
summary: Malkav's mad and prophetic children.

claims.text: Malkavians have Auspex, Dementation and Obfuscate.
Each Malkavian has a derangement, an imbalance of the humours, that can never be cured.

title: Nosferatu (Dark Ages)
summary: Cainites who wear the blood's corruption on their faces.

claims.text: Nosferatu have Animalism, Obfuscate and Potence.
Nosferatu have Appearance zero, which cannot be raised, and they fail first-impression rolls.

title: Ravnos (Dark Ages)
summary: Masters of illusion who cannot change their own nature.

claims.text: Ravnos have Animalism, Chimerstry and Fortitude.
Every Ravnos has a key personality trait, chosen at creation, that the Ravnos cannot change.

title: Followers of Set (Dark Ages)
summary: Children of Set, enemies of Horus.

claims.text: Setites have Obfuscate, Presence and Serpentis.
Setites carry Horus' curse and take twice the aggravated damage from sunlight.

title: Toreador (Dark Ages)
summary: Lovers of beauty with the shortest attention of all Cainites.

claims.text: Toreador have Auspex, Celerity and Presence.
Struck by beauty, a Toreador is held as if by Cupid's dart.

title: Tremere (Dark Ages)
summary: Upstart sorcerers who became a clan through the Amaranth.

claims.text: Tremere have Auspex, Dominate and Thaumaturgy.
Tremere are especially open to blood bonds when they drink other Cainites' blood.
The Tremere raided Saulot's tomb in 1133 and committed Amaranth on Saulot.

title: Tzimisce (Dark Ages)
summary: Lords who take their right to rule from the land itself.

claims.text: Tzimisce have Animalism, Auspex and Vicissitude.
A Tzimisce must rest with two handfuls of soil from a place important to the Tzimisce.
The Tzimisce share their blood with the earth and claim kingship from the land, not from heaven.

title: Ventrue (Dark Ages)
summary: Kings and lords of the Cainites.

claims.text: Ventrue have Dominate, Fortitude and Presence.
Each Ventrue can feed only on one kind of mortal, such as merchants, the French or Catholics.

title: Salubri
summary: Saulot's line, no longer counted a clan after the Tremere's crime.

claims.text: Noddist tales call Saulot Caine's most loved grandchilde, the only one Caine did not curse.
The Salubri hold themselves outside Cainite society and work to keep vampires and humans in balance.
Valeren, their own Discipline, has three paths: Healer, Warrior and Watcher.

title: Bloodlines of the Dark Medieval
summary: Lines outside the clans across Africa, Europe and Asia, such as the Anda, Baali, Kiasyd, Lhiannan and Salubri.

claims.text: Many bloodlines spread through Africa, Europe and Asia, some branched so far from their clan that they are no longer counted part of it.
The Gargoyles are built from the corpses of other vampires, most often Nosferatu, Gangrel and Tzimisce.
The Kiasyd's blood mixes fae magic with vitae.
The Lhiannan carry a shard of a great dark spirit of the land.

title: Abombwe
summary: The Bonsam's Discipline of primal darkness and predatory prowess.

claims.text: The Bonsam claim descent from a hunter possessed by an ancient darkness.

title: Bardo
summary: A Discipline said to come from Osiris, tied to the Road of Humanity.

claims.text: Bardo works by denying what the vampire is, where Golconda accepts and transcends it.

title: Daimonion
summary: The Baali's Discipline, an echo from the Abyss.

claims.text: Daimonion calls out across Creation to a forsaken place, and power returns with the echo.

title: Mytherceria
summary: The Kiasyd's Discipline that both hides and reveals truth.

claims.text: Mytherceria is rarely taught outside the Kiasyd.

title: Ogham
summary: The Lhiannan's variant of Koldunic Sorcery, named for the old script.

claims.text: Ogham is a form of Koldunic Sorcery named for the script needed to use it.

title: Spiritus
summary: The Ahrimanes' gift of speaking to spirits.

claims.text: The first Ahrimane learned to speak with animals from the goddess Freyja, and after death the gift reached the spirits of animals and objects.

title: Temporis
summary: The True Brujah's mastery of time.

claims.text: True Brujah say Temporis goes back to their Antediluvian and that Celerity is a poor copy.

title: Koldunic Sorcery
summary: The Tzimisce blood magic of the land and its spirits.

claims.text: The Tzimisce have mingled their blood and spirits with the earth of their lands since the First Days.

title: Blood Sorcery
summary: Abyss Mysticism, Koldunic Sorcery, Necromancy and Thaumaturgy: blood magic of paths and rituals.

claims.text: Blood Sorcery comes as paths, rituals or both, and each tradition has its own system.

title: Dark Medieval Italy
summary: By the 1240s Italy is a patchwork of growing cities where kine and Cainite thrive.

claims.text: By the middle of the 13th century Italy is a geographic name only; loyalty comes from the cities, swollen by migrants from the countryside.
